payload.build_machine:
FOUR CHUNKS, drawn to the M5 element boundaries so each is independently resumable if this run is interrupted.

c1 THE SEALED BRIEF (realization: engine-ts). New engine/brief.ts: seal/unseal (SP1's proven pair, iv|tag|ct, base64url fragment key), briefHtml (gate text -> escaped HTML), briefPage (ciphertext + inline decryptor reading location.hash), the BriefStore interface, publishBrief (seal -> put with bounded ttl -> CONFIRM IT SERVES -> return url#key, null on any failure), and KvBriefStore over the Workers KV account already verified live. Depends on: nothing. This is E2 whole, and it is the chunk carrying promoted code.

c2 THE TAPPABLE CARD (realization: engine-ts). engine/phone.ts: answerUrl absolutizing base+topic into a real http(s) URL, the card gaining title/priority/tags, the three-action budget with the third reserved for the brief, announceOffer returning a named AnnounceResult instead of void, and the transport built PER ANNOUNCE from freshly-read config. This is E1+E3+E4's card half, and it repairs the witnessed defect. Depends on: c1 (it consumes a brief URL) - but only at the type level, so it can be written in parallel and wired last.

c3 PUBLISH IFF THE RUN WAITS (realization: engine-ts). engine/wait.ts gains an onPark hook fired ONLY when an offer wait begins on a live offer; engine/tools.ts wires the real announcer into se_wait; bin/se-board.ts LOSES its announce timer and keeps only the tap poll. This is the owner's corrected rule made mechanical. Depends on: c2 (there must be something to fire).

c4 SAY WHAT HAPPENED (realization: engine-ts). Every announce records its outcome - success and failure - through the call log, and the degradation is named in the returned result. Depends on: c2. Small, and deliberately its own chunk rather than folded into c2: recording is the requirement whose absence let today's defect survive a day, and folding it into a bigger chunk is how it would get quietly dropped again.

PARALLELISM, honestly: c1 and c2 are independent and could fan out; c3 and c4 both wait on c2. This run builds them in sequence anyway - the whole build is small and one agent holds the context, so fanning out would cost more in coordination than it saves.
payload.promotions_placed:
SP1's seal/open pair enters as the FIRST content of c1, pre-verified rather than drafted - it is the code proven at run-e8599b7b7d2a, carried across in substance with only the change from a probe's inline script to a module's exported functions. Its four negative checks are already authored as permanent tests in the red suite, so the promotion arrives with its guard rather than trailing it.

SP2's finding is not code but a wiring decision, and it is placed as the whole of c3 - the trigger moves from the board's timer to the park seam.

The live transport probe (run-bfd564ff9add) contributes the exercised shapes of the KV put and the serve check, placed inside c1's KvBriefStore; v1's ask.go contributes the card shape placed inside c2.

Nothing is placed as 'to be tidied later', and the earlier throwaway probe script is explicitly not carried - it held the two crypto defects SP1 found.
